cases.customer_question: Does a product using the AzureWave AW-XM553 require Bluetooth RF and RF PHY qualification testing, or can it rely entirely on existing qualification reuse?
question_variants: Is AW-XM553 treated as a prequalified module or a SoC for Bluetooth qualification?
Do RF and RF PHY tests need to be performed for an AW-XM553-based design?
Can I avoid RF testing by reusing existing Bluetooth qualifications?
What qualification scope applies when using AW-XM553?
Does a SoC-based implementation require RF PHY testing?
cases.actual_issue: The qualification scope depends on whether the implementation is considered a reusable prequalified module solution or a SoC-based design. Review of the AW-XM553 datasheet led to the conclusion that the implementation should be treated as a SoC-based design requiring RF qualification testing.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Not all wireless modules qualify for simple qualification reuse. If the implementation is effectively based on a Bluetooth SoC rather than a fully reusable qualified module solution, Bluetooth radio testing may still be required. The qualification strategy must be based on the actual qualification status and architecture of the implementation.
cases.consultant_answer: After reviewing the AW-XM553 datasheet, the consultant determined that the implementation should be treated as a SoC-based design. Because of this classification, Bluetooth RF testing and RF PHY testing are required rather than relying solely on qualification reuse. The proposed qualification approach combines radio testing with a Multi-Design declaration strategy.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth qualification obligations are determined by the architecture and qualification status of the implementation. When the design is treated as a SoC implementation rather than a fully reusable qualified module solution, RF and RF PHY testing become required qualification elements.
cases.final_recommendation: Review the module architecture and qualification status carefully. If the implementation is determined to be SoC-based, plan for RF testing, RF PHY testing, and the appropriate qualification declaration process rather than assuming complete reuse eligibility.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Misclassifying a SoC-based implementation as fully reusable can result in omission of required RF and RF PHY testing, creating qualification compliance issues, declaration delays, and qualification rework.
